summary: Southwest Point light on Baccalieu Island, Newfoundland: a fog alarm from 1906, a light on a tower from 1953, unstaffed since 2002.

structures.note: CCG list: square skeleton tower, red and white rectangular daymark. Rowlett gives 3.5 m (12 ft) square cylindrical skeletal tower. LighthouseFriends describes a wooden pyramidal tower added in 1953.

access.note: Tower closed; grounds open. Seabird nesting areas closed in the season: 1 April to 30 October (LighthouseFriends) or May through October (Lighthouse Directory).

facts.agency: Canadian Coast Guard (owner, per LighthouseFriends); site manager Baccalieu Island Ecological Reserve (Lighthouse Directory)

events.note: Work began on a fog alarm station on the southwest tip of the island (LighthouseFriends)
Diaphone fog alarm began operation in August 1906 (LighthouseFriends); Lighthouse Directory gives the fog signal station established 1906
Light mounted atop a wooden pyramidal tower added to the southwest station (LighthouseFriends); light tower added 1953 (Lighthouse Directory)

corrections.why: The 1906 date is the diaphone fog alarm at the southwest station. The light was mounted on a tower in 1953 (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory).
LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse; the Lighthouse Directory names the Baccalieu Island Ecological Reserve as site manager.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory both describe a white flash every ten seconds; the Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights, as read on 28 October 2026, gives Fl W 4s (1 s flash, 3 s eclipse). The Coast Guard list is taken as the current source; the older descriptions are not reconciled further.

The 1906 date belongs to the fog alarm (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory). The light was added on a tower in 1953 (LighthouseFriends; Lighthouse Directory; the Coast Guard tower is the post-1953 structure).

notes_for_editor: Thin on history. Almost all the narrative (fog alarm 1905 and 1906, the 1953 light, the keeper list, the 2002 de-staffing, the 1840 and 1858 north-light history) rests on one page, LighthouseFriends, which credits its keeper list and some history to the Journal of the House of Assembly of Newfoundland and to the Encyclopedia of Newfoundland and Labrador, neither read here. The Canadian Department of Marine reports in the corpus cover Canada only, and Newfoundland was outside Canada until 1949, so no official primary report for 1905 to 1953 was checked. The US Life-Saving Service annual reports in the corpus list 'Baccalieu Island' among foreign places where US vessels were assisted (1892 to 1901), with no vessel or date tied to this light; not used. Keeper names: the north-end and southwest lists on the LighthouseFriends page share several surnames (Blundon, Hatch, Noonan, Hyde, and Eric Blundon appears on both). Nothing links the two lists; none is joined. The north-end light is a separate station with its own history (1858 tower, now CCG N-472 active light beside it). It needs its own record and was not researched here. The Lighthouse Directory calls the southwest tower 3.5 m; the Coast Guard list 4.3 m; the record's Wikidata figure is 4.3 m. The record's Wikidata characteristic 'Fl W 10s' is a lead only. Length: about 470 words of prose; the thin shape is used (no headings) because the history comes from one detailed page. The LighthouseFriends photographs and the Lighthouse Digest database were not used. Closure dates differ between sources and the story says so. Visitors are told to check reserve closure dates; the story does not encourage landing.
